messages:
Anya Patel: Pager fired — gateway-usw2: 5xx rate jumped to ~4.2% over last 3m, tailing off to 3.9% but still above alert. Seeing timeouts and 502/503s. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/INC-2145

devops-bot: Incident INC-2026-2145036789 created. Pager assigned to @oncall-sre. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/instruments/incident-runbook#gateway-5xx

oncall-sre: I'm on it. quick triage — is this a config/regression or upstream? any recent deploys to gateway cluster?

Anya Patel: No deploys to gateway in the last 30m. We had a canary rollout earlier today but that's in eu-central, not us-west. Traffic graph suggests spike correlates with an increase in client fanout from a small partner (agency-integ).

Callum Reed: I'm going to pull traces and check ingress proxies + edge fanout. Maria, can you validate if partner traffic has changed?

Maria Gomez: pinged partner ops. They confirm a release with a change to batch size at 21:15 UTC — might be sending larger requests. Also seeing a spike in avg seq length in logs.

Ravi Kumar: I'm seeing KV cache thrashing on the runtime side — latency per request doubled for many buckets. KV miss rate went from 6% -> 28% at the spike. Could explain timeouts upstream.

Anya Patel: ok mitigation plan: 1) temporarily reduce gateway concurrency/prefetch for that customer 2) enable stricter rate limiting for that partner route 3) roll queue backpressure to give runtime breathing room. Callum, can you push policy change?

Callum Reed: yes. Applying a targeted rate limit now for partner namespace (10rps -> 2rps) and setting worker concurrency to 4 for that route. Pushing patch:  
```bash
# temporary policy
redwoodctl routes update --route partner/agency-integ --rate-limit 2rps --concurrency 4
```

deploy-bot: Config change applied to gateway-usw2 (policy-id: tmp-2145-rl). No deploy required.

oncall-sre: After throttle: 5xx rate dropped to 1.1% in 90s. Latency tail improving. Marking mitigation as effective.

Anya Patel: Nice. Can we add a fallback model variant for large-seq requests to avoid KV pressure? If not immediate, at least add cache warm hints.

Ravi Kumar: I can add a KV prefetch for frequent prefixes for the partner for next 30m. Will trigger a quick warm run. Doing now.

Maria Gomez: Partner confirms reverting their batch-size change — they'll cut traffic over the next 10 minutes. They asked for our mitigation details. Shared temporary rate limit and expected restore plan.

Callum Reed: Quick note: we saw a secondary cause — an edge proxy started queuing long-running POSTs and hit a connection pool limit. I bumped pool_size on proxy nodes from 100 -> 200 as a hotpatch. That reduced 504s. Command:  
```yaml
# hotspot change applied via chef
proxy_pool_size: 200
```

oncall-sre: All checks green. 5xx down to 0.6% and back to baseline in the last 4m. Closing pager but keeping thread open for follow-ups and RCA.

Anya Patel: Customer impact: limited to partner agency-integ (approx 1200 requests/min peak). No broad customer outages. Support to email affected customers? @support-bot can you draft a short note?

support-bot: Drafted message: "We briefly throttled traffic for partner integration due to elevated error rates. The issue was mitigated and normal service restored. If you experienced errors between 21:20-21:35 UTC, please reply and we will investigate. — Redwood SRE" Sending to oncall for approval.

Callum Reed: Action items before we close: 
- [Anya] confirm runbook additions for partner-induced seq-length spikes
- [Ravi] make KV-prefetch script into a one-click ops play
- [Maria] follow up with partner and confirm revert timeline
- [SRE] tune alert thresholds to reduce noisy paging
- [Infra] consider default proxy pool_size bump and rollout plan

I'll annotate PRs and owners below.

Anya Patel: I'll update runbook now. Proposed edits: add section "Partner burst handling" with steps: add targeted rate-limit, apply worker concurrency cap, enable cache-warm, and proxy pool check. Also add playbook snippet.

Anya Patel: Proposed runbook snippet:  
```text
# Partner burst handling
1) Identify partner namespace + recent deploys
2) Apply temporary rate limit: redwoodctl routes update --route <partner> --rate-limit 2rps
3) Reduce worker concurrency: --concurrency 4
4) Warm KV cache: /ops/kv-warm --prefix <partner-prefix>
5) If proxy 504s persist: bump proxy_pool_size and alert infra
6) Notify partner + support
```

Ravi Kumar: I'll turn my ad-hoc warm script into a playbook and PR it — target: today EOD. PR: https://git.redwood/ops/kv-warm/-/merge_requests/142

Maria Gomez: Partner confirmed full revert at 21:33 UTC and saw normal traffic by 21:36. I'm scheduling a 1:1 with their infra lead to tune client-side batch sizing.

Callum Reed: Alert tuning notes: current alert uses simple 1m percent_5xx > 3%. We should move to 3m rolling, require >= 2 clusters affected, and add a partner-fanout suppressor to avoid paging for single-tenant spikes. I'll open ticket.

Anya Patel: Filing follow-up tickets and owners:
- RUNBOOK-271: add "Partner burst handling" section (owner: Anya) — due: tomorrow 17:00 UTC
- OPS-842: build kv-warm playbook + one-click (owner: Ravi) — due: EOD
- ALERTS-510: adjust 5xx alert window & add partner suppressor (owner: Callum) — due: 2d
- INFRA-301: analyze default proxy pool_size bump (owner: infra team) — due: 3d

Callum Reed: I'll also add a short postmortem note summarizing root cause + mitigations in the incident doc.

oncall-sre: Closing the pager. If anything regresses please reopen. Great cross-team response. :tada:

Anya Patel: Thanks team. Logging this thread into the incident tracker and attaching graphs. Will follow up with a short RCA later today.
